## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin white to pale gray thallus with fine striations or streaked texture, often forming smooth, blanket-like patches across bark. In Florida, it is found growing on tree trunks, branches, and other bark surfaces in humid forests, hammocks, swamps, shaded parks, and other moist wooded habitats. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing tightly attached to bark and absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on the tree itself.
